To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the use of social networking sites is associated with a greater neuroticism profile, a greater impulsivity profile, lower academic self-esteem, lower family self-esteem and lower emotional self-esteem, greater perceived family consumption of ICT, greater perceived consumption of ICT by the mother, greater perceived consumption by siblings, lower perceived family norms for the use of ICT and lower perceived family norms of ICT use.
the prevalence of SNS overuse was 12.8% being higher in girls.
In summary, our research is concerned with
exploring the psychological and social profiles of adolescents who engage in excessive social networking use.
the study of the psychosocial profile of adolescents who use social networks excessively.
the identification of the psychosocial profile of young people who use social media in an extreme way.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of social networks in adolescents is associated to the personality of the adolescent, the family and the environment.
the excessive use of social networks is related to the personality of adolescents and to their perception of the use of social networks by their family and friends.
excessive use of SNS in adolescence is related with neuroticism, impulsiveness, low self-concept in family, academic, and emotional aspects, and high perception of SNS use by parents and siblings.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the excessive use of social networks is associated with personality traits (neuroticism and impulsivity) and social factors (perceived use of TIC in the family and the absence of rules for the use of TIC at home) in adolescents.
excessive use of social networking in adolescence is related to neuroticism, impulsiveness and a lack of social support.
we have identified a profile of personality and social factors that characterize the adolescents with excessive use of social networks.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of social networking sites (SNS) is a complex phenomenon that requires a multidimensional approach.
it is possible to predict who is at risk of excessive use of social networks in adolescence and, thus, to design prevention strategies that target the most vulnerable groups.
the excessive use of social networks by adolescents is related to a personality profile characterized by neuroticism and impulsivity, and low academic and emotional self-concept.
